models_evaluated: parameter-transferred Wasserstein generative adversarial network (PET denoising)

links.outcome: Lesion detection by physician readers on AI-denoised low-dose PET versus full-dose reference, despite good image-quality metrics
links.effect: Image quality rated good/excellent in 32/33 PET_AI; but sensitivity 66% (78/118), false discovery rate 32% (37/115); 62% (23/37) of FPs scored as definite lesions.
links.quote: However, lesion detection analysis performed by physicians showed high proportions of FP and FN lesions on PET<sub>AI</sub>, highlighting the need for clinical validation of AI algorithms.

screen.reason: The study conducts a clinical reader study evaluating physician lesion detection and diagnostic safety on GAN-denoised low-dose PET images, revealing significant false-positive and false-negative rates.
